title: control-room handoff
description: A worker's claim about its epic: `handoff/<epic>.json` on the epic's branch, one file per epic, changed as the epic moves. It is a claim, not an authority: the coordinator reads it at the READY sha and checks it against the tracker and the recorded check run, and trusts the run record over this copy of it. The validator checks this schema and what a schema cannot state: the file is named for its `epic`; a `ready` handoff carries a `lane` whose verdict is `passed` and no child still `open`; a `deferred` child has a `note` and a `reparented` one a `to`; the branch carries the configured prefix; every sha is 40 hex characters.

epic.description: The epic's bead id. The file's name without `.json` must equal it.

profile.description: The worker profile the epic is assigned to: one of the profiles the project declares (control-room.json).

session.description: The cloud session the assignment names. the landing check compares the two, because two sessions of one profile can exist and the profile alone does not say which one did the work.

branch.description: `<prefix><epic>-<slug>`, created from the integration branch by the epic's first commit. The prefix is the project's `branch_prefix` (control-room.json, default `claude/`), which the validator checks because it is configuration, not schema.

status.description: `working` from the first commit. `blocked` while it waits on `questions`, and the session ends `EPIC <id> BLOCKED <reason>`. `ready` only in the branch's last commit, S, written after the run finished, and the session ends `EPIC <id> READY <S> <pr-url>`.

children.description: Every child of the epic, and what became of it. `open` is a working state and never a ready one: the validator refuses a `ready` handoff with an `open` child, and the landing check refuses the landing.

outcome.description: `done`: finished in this branch, and the landing closes it. `deferred`: not done here and left open for later, with the reason in `note` (required, checked by the validator). `reparented`: belongs under another epic, named in `to` (required, checked the same way). `open`: not yet decided, which is allowed only before `ready`.

commits.description: Full shas of the commits that did it. A short sha can become ambiguous in a repository that keeps growing.

to.description: For `reparented`: the bead the child moves under.

discovered.description: Work found while doing this epic that is not part of it. Workers never write beads, so this is where a new bead comes from: the coordinator files each entry when it lands the epic.

questions.description: What the worker needs the coordinator or the person to answer. A `blocked` handoff is blocked on the ones marked `blocking`. The answer comes back as a message into the session, not as an edit to this file.

shared_change_requests.description: Changes this epic needs in paths outside its scope and grants: another profile's, or one the coordinator holds. The worker does not make them; it names the paths and says why, and the coordinator relays each one.

runs.description: The ids of this epic's harness runs, its run among them. the landing check reads each one from S, and the run files, not this list, are what it believes.

lane.description: A copy of the finished run's lane result, written after `--finish`. Required when `status` is `ready`, which the validator checks because the schema cannot. the landing check reads the run file, not this copy.

seconds.description: The run's `gates.seconds`: the lane's wall clock.

head.description: The run's `gates.head`: the commit the lane ran at. S may differ from it only by handoff and run files.

gates.description: The run's `gates.results`, id and outcome only.

base.description: The full sha of the integration branch the worker last merged before READY.
